messages:
nina: flagging a customer report: embedded streaming sessions sometimes show "confirmed" tokens but the client claims it never saw the final chunk. billing spike -> support ticket.
owen: got the ticket, saw the trace. router logs show a truncated EOF followed by a reconnect; the replay created a separate toolcall and confirmed both.
raj: is the router using the same confirmation handshake semantics for toolcalls vs vanilla streams? iirc toolcalls confirm on tool response end, streams confirm on EOF.
liz: yes, two different code paths. earlier kludge treated short disconnects as retries and replayed bytes, but that interacts badly with confirm-on-ack versus confirm-on-eof.
nina: customer scenario: mobile client loses cellular for 7s, reconnects with resume token, gets rest of the stream. they saw tokens marked confirmed at 2 different ledger entries.
owen: sample request headers from trace_176989: 
```
POST /v1/chat/stream
Host: api.redwood
X-Resume-Token: r-7a12
X-Client-Beta: true
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
```
raj: two immediate ideas: unify confirmation semantics (confirm only on final EOF for both toolcalls and streams) or keep semantics but add a dedupe pass when resume token matches and prefix bytes overlap.
liz: unify sounds safer for accounting correctness but has perf/latency implications: some toolcall workflows expect confirmation earlier to charge third-party tool usage.
nina: agree. Also need console visibility so Support can quickly see "ambiguous confirmed tokens" and the two ledger ids side-by-side. right now the console shows two separate invoices and no indication they're likely duplicates.
owen: propose a three-pronged plan: 1) short-term console flag + API to mark a ledger entry as "under review" for ops 2) router change to prefer resume-token de-duplication for N seconds after disconnect 3) longer-term API unification design doc to align confirm semantics for toolcalls and streams.
raj: for (1) schema for ledger patch: do we allow manual annotate via console that writes an AuditNote? billing team insisted on immutable ledgers but will accept a reconciliation event record. we can write a ReconcileRecord event that references original ledger ids.
liz: agree on ReconcileRecord. minimal fields: ledger_ids (list), reason, operator, timestamp. we need to keep it flat for exports.
nina: UX idea: in route billing page show a small "Orphan Confirmations" table and allow ops to select pairs and click "Reconcile" which triggers ReconcileRecord and issues a corrective credit if needed.
owen: technical quirk: we must ensure reconciliation idempotency. if two ops click reconcile on same pair, avoid double credits. add reconciler service that checks an existing ReconcileRecord before applying.
raj: for router dedupe: implement a best-effort prefix-match algorithm: when resume-token matches, check last provisional bytes for overlap > X bytes and mark subsequent confirmation as merge instead of new confirmed. risk: false merges on coincidental prefixes. threshold tuning required.
liz: add telemetry: expose a metric "reconcile_candidates" with labels route/model and a histogram of overlap bytes. console can graph that to help tune threshold.
nina: billing-bot what would a ReconcileRecord look like in the ledger?
billing-bot: ReconcileRecord prototype: {"type":"reconcile","id":"rec_<ts>","ledgers":["l_123","l_124"],"operator":"liz","reason":"duplicate-confirmation-due-to-resume","credit_amount":"-0.42"} (example)
raj: note we can't have nested JSON in the reconcile event payloads for export, must keep fields flat; we can stringify arrays as comma-separated in the event.
owen: action items: owen -> console flag + reconcile API (canary) ; raj -> router dedupe POC and metric; liz -> billing reconciliation workflow and docs; nina -> own support backlog and coordinate with customer.
liz: timeline: console flag in 48h, router POC next week, reconcile job after we validate POC.
nina: also notify product: customers will want a one-off credit for impacted invoice. product needs to approve manual credits.
owen: ok I'll open a small PR and post deploy when canary is up.
billing-bot: billing: created reconciliation-ticket/TKT-8421, notify billing@redwood.
raj: one more thought7 we might consider adding a small resume checksum header on client SDKs so router can match streams deterministically. long-term work.
liz: yep. SDK change tracked in devex backlog.
nina: thanks all. keep updates in this thread and paste trace ids.
